5.text: Oracle shares have fallen sharply—down 28% to 59% this year—even as its AI contract backlog swells toward $664 billion and cloud growth accelerates. Analysts call the stock undervalued, and Tencent reportedly signed a $7 billion, five-year Oracle cloud deal.

7.text: Ten market-research reports forecast growth across enterprise IT, AI, cloud, integration, and security segments through 2030–2031, with Oracle named among vendors benchmarked in most. Only the healthcare AI report omits Oracle.

8.text: Bloom Energy shares swung sharply on Oracle’s Project Jupiter force majeure notice, then rebounded as Jefferies raised its target to $264 and RBC reiterated $335. CEO Sridhar said Bloom boxes are “fungible,” so a project delay wouldn’t concern the company.

4.text: Oracle’s Project Jupiter, an $18 billion New Mexico AI data center, faces reported delays, a force majeure notice, and flooding, though Oracle says it remains on schedule. Oracle’s AI-driven cloud growth is accompanied by heavy capex, negative free cash flow, rising debt and credit risk tied to OpenAI reliance.

9.text: Oracle’s founder increased his stock-backed borrowing, and Oracle was among the most-searched tickers on Benzinga Pro in September. Otherwise, the articles cover broad market moves, Treasury yields, and other companies.

10.text: Adobe trades at 13x earnings, down 33% over twelve months, with 12% revenue growth and a 58% drop from its 2024 high. Microsoft returned 37% in three months at a 28.3 P/E; Oracle isn't mentioned.

6.text: Oracle Japan shares rose 7% after reporting record fiscal first-quarter sales and profits, outperforming its U.S. parent's stock selloff.
